flipmeta

flipmeta performs robust score tests for models fitted with metafor by randomly sign-flipping study-level score contributions. It supports both a single meta-analytic model and a collection of related model specifications that share the same studies.

For a collection of models, flipmeta keeps each study’s random sign aligned across every specification in which that study appears. The resulting joint randomization distribution can then be used to adjust p-values for testing multiple specifications or coefficients.

[!IMPORTANT] flipmeta is currently experimental. The public API and returned object structure may change before version 1.0.0.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub with:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("livioivil/flipscores")
remotes::install_github("filippogambarota/flipmeta")

The explicit installation of flipscores is currently needed because it is a GitHub dependency.

A single meta-analysis

The input must be a model fitted by metafor::rma.uni(). Use tested_coeffs to select the coefficients to test.

library(flipmeta)

dat <- data.frame(
  study_id = paste0("study", 1:12),
  yi = c(.12, .31, -.04, .27, .08, .36, .15, .42, .02, .24, .19, .33),
  vi = c(.04, .05, .03, .06, .04, .07, .05, .06, .03, .05, .04, .07),
  dose = rep(c(0, 1), 6),
  quality = rep(c("high", "low", "high"), 4)
)

fit <- metafor::rma.uni(
  yi,
  vi,
  mods = ~ dose,
  data = dat
)

set.seed(2026)
result <- flipmeta(
  fit,
  B = 999,
  tested_coeffs = "dose"
)

result$summary_table
plot(result)

Here B = 999 keeps the example quick. Use more sign flips for a final analysis; the default is B = 5000. You can also pass a precomputed matrix to flips when the exact randomization distribution must be reused.

The main result columns are:

  • estimate and se: estimates from the fitted metafor model;
  • statistic: the observed standardized score statistic;
  • score: the unstandardized observed score;
  • tau2_null: heterogeneity estimated under the coefficient-specific null;
  • p: the sign-flip p-value.

Multiple model specifications

Pass a named list of rma.uni models to test related specifications jointly. The id column must identify studies uniquely and must be created before any filtering or reordering.

fits <- list(
  all = fit,
  high_quality = metafor::rma.uni(
    yi,
    vi,
    mods = ~ dose,
    data = dat,
    subset = quality == "high"
  )
)

choices <- data.frame(
  selection = c("All studies", "High quality only")
)

set.seed(2026)
joint <- flipmeta(
  fits,
  id = "study_id",
  B = 999,
  tested_coeffs = "dose",
  extra = choices,
  progress = FALSE
)

joint$summary_table

Studies absent from a specification receive a zero score contribution in that model, while the same study retains the same random sign across models.

Multiple-testing adjustment

Use flipmeta::p.adjust() to adjust results using their joint randomization distribution. Qualifying the function with flipmeta:: avoids ambiguity with stats::p.adjust().

joint_adjusted <- flipmeta::p.adjust(joint, method = "maxT")
joint_adjusted$summary_table

plot(joint_adjusted)
spec_curve(joint_adjusted)

Adjustments can also be performed separately within families defined by columns of the result table:

joint_adjusted <- flipmeta::p.adjust(
  joint,
  by = "coefficient",
  method = "maxT"
)

Main functions

Function Purpose
flipmeta() Run a sign-flip score test on one or more rma.uni models
flipmeta::p.adjust() Adjust p-values using the joint flip distribution
plot() Plot estimates against raw or adjusted p-values
spec_curve() Plot a specification curve for a joined analysis
transf_p() Transform p-values for plotting
combine_tests() Combine tests using functionality from flipscores
combine_contrasts() Combine contrasts using functionality from flipscores

See ?flipmeta and the help page for each function for argument and return-value details.

Scope and limitations

  • Supported inputs are univariate models produced by metafor::rma.uni(); multivariate rma.mv models are not supported.
  • Available heterogeneity estimators are "REML", "ML", "DL", and "EE"(equal-effects model).
  • Monte Carlo p-values depend on the generated flips. Set a seed or supply flips to make an analysis exactly reproducible.
  • For a model list, missing, duplicated, or model-specific identifiers are rejected because they could invalidate alignment across specifications.
  • A numerically degenerate flip-specific variance produces an error rather than silently changing the p-value denominator.

Development

Run the test suite with:

testthat::test_local()

Run a full local package check with:

R CMD build . --no-build-vignettes --no-manual
R CMD check flipmeta_0.1.0.tar.gz --no-manual --no-build-vignettes

Bug reports and reproducible examples are welcome in the GitHub issue tracker.
